chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Sa‘īd ibn ‘Umar al-Jullāb, from al-Ḥārith al-A‘war, who said:

‘Ali (peace be upon him) said: May I sacrifice my father and mother for al-Ḥusayn, the one killed on the outskirts of Kūfah. By Allah, it is as if I can see the wild beasts stretching their necks towards his grave, from various kinds of beasts, weeping for him and mourning him throughout the night until dawn. When this happens, beware of neglect (him/his grave).
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wild animals weeping at the grave of Imam al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This narration from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the Shia belief in the cosmic resonance of al-Ḥusayn’s martyrdom, where the natural world participates in his mourning as a sign of divine recognition. The term 'al-Jafā’ (hardness of heart or neglect) serves as a practical spiritual warning for believers to maintain emotional and devotional connection with the Ahl al-Bayt, lest they become spiritually insensitive to this ongoing celestial event.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 2. My father and ‘Ali ibn Ḥusain both narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Aḥmad ibn Abī Dāwūd, from Sa’d ibn (Abī) ‘Amr Al-Jallāb, from Ḥārith Al-A’war (Al-Hamdāni), who said:

‘Ali, (the Commander of the Believers (a.s.)), said: May I sacrifice my father and mother for Ḥusain who will be killed on the outskirts of Kūfah. I swear to Allāh that it is as if I can see the different kinds of wild animals stretching their necks to his grave, crying and weeping over him throughout the night until dawn. When this happens, beware of neglecting him (his grave).
